newsitem.title: LATVIA: FOCUS - LITHUANIA EUROBOND NOT SEEN HITTING LOCAL MARKET.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - LITHUANIA EUROBOND NOT SEEN HITTING LOCAL MARKET.

text.p: Lithuania's $200 million eurobond, launched on Tuesday, will probably not have a big impact on the local debt market, dealers and analysts said on Tuesday.

The finance ministry has stated that one of its goals in tapping the international capital markets is to reduce its borrowing costs and attract more foreign investors to its local debt and equity markets.
But dealers said that there did not appear to be much scope for Treasury bill yields to fall further and said the bond would have limited impact on the local market.
"Interest rates are at their real level right now and should not fall too much further," said one dealer.
Lithuania set the five-year bond, which is lead managed by J.P. Morgan, at 105 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
It was the country's second foray into the eurobond market.
Rates on Lithuanian T-bills have been falling, with the average yield for Tuesday's six-month issue dropping to 9.18 percent from 9.64 percent.
"If rates fall much further, demand will dry up pretty fast," said one dealer.
But another dealer said that rates could fall some more although the eurobond issue would not be the cause.

"Yields can fall some more, because the market is dominated by Lithuanian commercial banks. They have a lot of money to throw around right now, and don't know where else to invest it," said one dealer.
"Demand could keep going up and yields could come down some more, but it won't be driven by foreigners...it will be local," the dealer said.
"Foreign investors are more interested now in Lithuanian bond issues in foreign currencies than in the local T-bill market...there are still some concerns about the stability of the litas," he said.
Lithuania might set another bond this year but given its modest borrowing requirements, analysts do not expect it to bring very much paper before the international capital markets.
